questions.title: Who will succeed Brendon McCullum as permanent head coach of England's men's Test team?
questions.background: Brendon McCullum currently coaches England's men's Test cricket team.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official England and Wales Cricket Board appointment announcement or reliable contemporaneous reporting of that announcement. Resolution : Resolve to the first person formally appointed as McCullum's permanent successor as head coach of England's men's Test team. Interim appointments and appointments solely concerning limited-overs cricket do not count. Resolution occurs when the appointment is announced, even if the coach begins work later. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-17 update: frontrunner Andy Flower publicly and formally ruled himself out of the England Test head coach race at London Spirit's media day (BBC Sport, Sky Sports, Reuters, ESPNcricinfo, Hindustan Times), confirming he turned down the ECB even with dual-role IPL flexibility because IPL/RCB duties clash with the early English summer. Following Flower's withdrawal, iNews Cricket Correspondent Chris Stocks reports on July 17 that the ECB is now pivoting to former Australia coach Justin Langer as its top target (rated 4/5; strong Ashes rebuilding pedigree and county familiarity, though tempered by LSG IPL ties and past intensity concerns), lifting Langer 0.13 -> 0.26. Newly available Stephen Fleming (co-rated 4/5 by iNews, named by BBC Sport July 17) rises 0.19 -> 0.25 as he just left CSK after 18 years—removing the IPL clash that deterred Flower—was Rob Key's 2022 preference, and publicly welcomed an approach this week. Among remaining shortlisted contenders, Jonathan Trott (0.15 -> 0.16, English, available, named by BBC Sport/iNews 3/5), Richard Dawson (0.07 -> 0.09, English, ECB pathway, named by BBC Sport July 17), and Tom Moody (new entry at 0.07, explicitly named by BBC Sport July 17 alongside Trott, Dawson, and Fleming) round out the top 5, leaving 17% residual for Kumar Sangakkara, Mike Hesson, Adi Birrell, and unlisted options as BBC notes the ECB is still in an initial stage and open to an interim for August's Pakistan series.

local_articles.title: Kevin Pietersen throws his weight behind ex-teammate Jonathan Trott as England look for Brendon McCullum’s replacement
local_articles.snippet: Board (ECB) moves heaven and earth to find a new Test head coach after sacking Brendon McCullum last week from that role, former England batsman Kevin Pietersen has come out in support of ex-teammate Jonathan Trott and hopes he is the replacement for the New Zealander in red-ball cricket. {{^htLoading}} {{/htLoading}} From 2009-2015, 45-year-old Trott played 52 Tests, 68 ODIs and 7 T20Is. He won three Ashes and scored a match-winning second-innings century on debut in the time-honoured contest. In the 2010-11 Ashes, he played a big part in England winning the contest in Australia after a long gap of 24 years. The right-handed batsman was also part of the team that stunned India in India in 2012-13. At present, he is a short-term consultant with Ireland. questions.title: Which country will win the men's team gymnastics gold medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games?
questions.background: The Commonwealth Games men's team gymnastics competition awards medals according to the final team standings.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Commonwealth Games results, corroborated by contemporary reliable news reporting. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the country awarded gold in the men's team gymnastics competition at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, once the final standings are announced. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the winning country.
questions.current_reasoning: Two major developments since June 24 significantly narrow the England-Canada gap ahead of the July 24 Glasgow 2026 men's team final: (1) Three-time Olympic champion Max Whitlock withdrew on July 13 with a hand injury sustained in training (BBC Sport, Reuters), removing an elite pommel horse specialist and disrupting England's late-stage lineup, while Team England's Chef de Mission noted the squad mixes Olympic/world medallists with several multi-sport debutants; (2) Gymnastics Canada officially named a powerhouse A-team on July 3—Paris Olympians Félix Dolci, René Cournoyer, and William Émard plus Jordan Carroll and Ethan Ikeda—fresh off winning historic team gold at the 2026 Pan American Championships (with Émard winning rings gold and Carroll pommel horse silver). England remains the clear favorite given its unmatched all-around/apparatus depth and three straight CWG team titles, but trims 0.74 -> 0.64 while Canada jumps sharply 0.13 -> 0.25; Australia (young squad, 4 debutants) trims 0.06 -> 0.05, Cyprus holds 0.03, and host Scotland trims 0.03 -> 0.02 (1% residual).

questions.title: Which club will Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha join after Chaves in 2026?
questions.background: Vozinha is a Cape Verde international goalkeeper. Chaves is a Portuguese football club.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official club or player announcement, or reliable contemporaneous sports reporting confirming a completed move. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the first club Vozinha joins after leaving Chaves in 2026. Offers, negotiations, and proposed transfers do not count. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the club.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-17 breaking transfer update from Bolavip Brasil citing TyC Sports journalist Germán García Grova and UOL Esporte's Samir Carvalho: Chilean giants Colo-Colo have submitted an official offer to free-agent Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha (an initial 6-month contract through December 2026 with automatic target-based renewal through end of 2027), and Vozinha has reportedly approved Colo-Colo's terms, leaving the signing very close to completion. The same report notes Corinthians rejected the keeper, while inquiries from Ceará, Avaí, and Atlético Goianiense did not progress and Inter Miami remained speculative (though Al Jazeera still mentioned Inter Miami interest on July 17). Promoting Colo-Colo to #1 at a disciplined 0.52—respecting the anti-overconfidence cap until officially signed and announced—while cutting Inter Miami 0.28 -> 0.12, Ceara 0.14 -> 0.04, Avai 0.05 -> 0.02, and Atletico Goianiense 0.03 -> 0.02 (28% residual if Colo-Colo talks collapse or another club hijacks).

questions.title: Who will be appointed Peru's foreign minister in the incoming presidential administration's first cabinet in July 2026?
questions.background: A new presidential administration is scheduled to take office in Peru in July 2026. Its foreign minister will oversee the country's diplomatic relations.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Peruvian government announcements or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the person officially appointed minister of foreign affairs in the incoming administration's first cabinet, with the appointment announced by July 31, 2026. Speculation about potential appointments does not count. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed foreign minister's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Key transition updates through 2026-07-12 ahead of Keiko Fujimori's July 28 inauguration: (1) Officially proclaimed winner on July 3, Fujimori accredited her formal Ministry of Foreign Affairs transfer team (ETTE) on July 7-8 led by corporate/tax lawyers Carlos Saco-Vértiz Tudela and Carla Mares Ruiz—an administrative audit team rather than a diplomat-in-waiting—while El Comercio and Caretas (July 8) report she will announce her Premier/Cabinet chief only after receiving physical JNE credentials on July 15; (2) Treating outgoing Balcázar FM Carlos Pareja Ríos purely as the outgoing counterpart receiving the transition audit reduces his retention odds (0.10 -> 0.06); (3) Peruvian outlet Off The Record (June 29) circulated former conservative FM Javier González-Olaechea Franco as the rumored Foreign Minister in 'Gabinete K'—still an unconfirmed single-source rumor warranting a calibrated bump (0.07 -> 0.12) narrowly ahead of career diplomats Hugo de Zela (held at 0.11; resigned cleanly from Balcázar in April though linked to the Nov 2025 Mexico rupture as Fujimori signaled July 10 she wants to restore Mexico ties) and Elmer Schialer (0.06 -> 0.07), with Alfredo Ferrero held at 0.05 and 59% tail mass retained for Torre Tagle's deep diplomatic bench.

questions.title: Who will be the first West Indies bowler to take a five-wicket haul in the opening Test against Pakistan in Tarouba in July 2026?
questions.background: A five-wicket haul means that a bowler takes at least five wickets in a single innings.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the first West Indies bowler to reach five wickets in a single innings during the opening Test against Pakistan in Tarouba in July 2026, according to the match scorecard and contemporaneous match reporting. Resolution Date : 2026-07-27 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the bowler's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: The opening Test at Brian Lara Cricket Academy in Tarouba (July 25-29) will be the venue's maiden Test match, expected to offer seam movement and variable bounce. West Indies' June 16 Test squad for Sri Lanka confirms CWI's managed pace trio of Jayden Seales (Trinidad home bowler and WI's most reliable strike seamer), Shamar Joseph (51 Test wickets at 21.67, returning from shoulder injury), and Alzarri Joseph (returning from back injury), alongside vice-captain and sole specialist spinner Jomel Warrican (19 wickets vs Pakistan in 2025) and veteran Kemar Roach. Conditional on a West Indies bowler claiming a five-for, Seales (29%) and Shamar Joseph (27%) lead as primary new-ball/strike threats, with 10% left for Roston Chase, Anderson Phillip, Justin Greaves, or a recalled Gudakesh Motie.

questions.title: Which Southeast Asian country will announce a finalized voluntary repatriation plan for thousands of Myanmar refugees in August 2026?
questions.background: Repatriation means returning refugees to their country of origin. This question concerns finalization of a government plan, rather than the completion of refugee returns.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government statements or reliable news reporting directly quoting those statements. Resolving Event : During August 2026, a Southeast Asian government publicly confirms that it has finalized a voluntary repatriation programme, or the first phase of such a programme, covering at least 1,000 refugees from Myanmar. A preliminary agreement to consider returns is insufficient. Actual departures need not have occurred. Accepted Answer Format : The common English name of the country finalizing the repatriation plan, not the destination country.
questions.current_reasoning: Only Southeast Asian countries qualify (excluding Bangladesh), and Thailand and Malaysia host over 95% of Myanmar refugees in Southeast Asia. Thailand hosts 80,155 registered camp refugees, is actively implementing a border camp-closure timeline announced in May-June 2026, has prior UNHCR voluntary-return precedent, and enjoys the closest ties with Min Aung Hlaing's April 2026 administration. Malaysia hosts ~190,000 UNHCR-registered Myanmar refugees (mostly Rohingya) and on June 22, 2026 PM Anwar Ibrahim and Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman explicitly vowed direct engagement with Myanmar authorities on repatriation, making Malaysia a close second, with Indonesia (~2,000-3,000 Rohingya) a distant third.

questions.title: Which Federal Reserve policymakers will vote for an interest-rate increase at the July 29, 2026 FOMC meeting?
questions.background: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets US monetary policy. Its policy announcements disclose members' votes and the policy preferences of dissenting voters.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Federal Reserve's official policy statement and voting record for the meeting concluding July 29, 2026, corroborated by contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution : Identify every voting member whose recorded position favors increasing the federal funds target range relative to the range immediately before the meeting. Include those members whether an increase is adopted or they dissent in favor of one. Accepted Answer Format : All qualifying members' surnames, listed alphabetically and separated by commas.
questions.current_reasoning: Second consecutive day of cooler-than-expected US inflation data on 2026-07-15 (Reuters/Korea Times, Straits Times, Axios): June headline PPI unexpectedly fell -0.3% MoM (vs. 0.0% consensus; May revised sharply down from +1.1% to +0.6%), slowing YoY PPI to 5.5% from 6.0%, while core PPI ex-food/energy/trade rose just +0.1% MoM (pointing to ~0.2% MoM / 3.3% YoY core PCE). Following the PPI print and Chair Kevin Warsh's two days of Capitol Hill testimony—where he welcomed inflation 'going in the right direction' and previewed an upcoming 'good family fight' over timing rather than signaling an imminent hike—CME FedWatch July 29 rate-hike odds fell further to 10.2% (89.8% hold, down from 12%-17% July 14 and 31% a week ago). With majority-hike odds shrinking to ~10% and Continuum Economics emphasizing 'no more than two hawkish dissents' led by Cleveland's Beth Hammack and Dallas's Lorie Logan (with Minneapolis's Neel Kashkari less likely), shifting weight toward solo 'Hammack' (0.19 -> 0.22) and 'Hammack, Logan' (0.17 -> 0.18), trimming the 3-way 'Hammack, Kashkari, Logan' (0.08 -> 0.06), and holding solo 'Logan' (0.05) and 'Hammack, Kashkari' (0.03), leaving 46% outside the top 5 for unanimous hold, majority-hike coalitions, and other dissent sets ahead of the July 18 FOMC blackout.

questions.title: In which country outside Iran, if any, will US forces strike Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026?
questions.background: Iran-aligned armed groups operate across several Middle Eastern countries, creating potential flashpoints for military confrontation with the United States.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera, supported where available by official military statements. Resolution Conditions : Identify the country outside Iran where US forces conduct strikes against Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026, inclusive. Direct US participation in either unilateral or joint strikes qualifies; threats, proposed operations, and diplomatic support do not. Accepted Answer Format : The country's name, or “None” if no qualifying strikes occur.
questions.current_reasoning: Sharp 2026-07-17 escalation across Al Jazeera, Reuters, and Hindustan Times pushes strike risk higher ahead of the July 22-29 window and trims the peaceful 'None' baseline. US forces launched a 6th and 7th consecutive night of strikes on Iran (hitting bridges, rail, Bandar Abbas, Yazd, Sirik, and damaging sites inside Bushehr), while Iran struck a Kuwait power and water plant and targeted US assets across Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Iraq, Jordan, and Syria. Supreme Leader adviser Maj.-Gen. Mohsen Rezaei warned July 17 that Tehran will launch 'full-scale offensive operations' if US strikes continue another 2-3 days ('no political border will be safe'), while Trump repeated threats to strike Iranian power plants next week—the exact trigger for Tehran's order putting Yemen's Houthis on standby to close Bab al-Mandeb (with mass Houthi rallies in Sanaa on July 17 and a $2bn US arms sale to Saudi Arabia approved July 16). Lifting Yemen 0.36 -> 0.39 to slight #1. In Iraq, Al Jazeera reported coalition air defenses intercepted 8 explosive drones over Erbil near the US consulate on July 16 and the Islamic Resistance in Iraq announced a $10M Trump assassination bounty on July 17, lifting Iraq 0.21 -> 0.24. Cutting None 0.38 -> 0.31 (still substantial given US focus on Iran proper and potential diplomacy/Saudi burden-sharing), holding Lebanon 0.03, and nudging Syria 0.01 -> 0.02 after reported IRGC targeting of US assets there.

local_articles.title: Iran supreme leader warns of ‘unforgettable lessons’ if US attacks continue
local_articles.snippet: called on Iranians to trust the leadership to protect the country, urging people to remain “vigilant” and “active” as the fighting grinds on. Reports have surfaced in recent days that the Houthis in Yemen could close the Bab al-Mandeb gateway to the Red Sea in support of their crucial ally Iran. That would further destabilise global energy markets, increase inflation and apply additional pressure on Trump to halt attacks. The war is deeply unpopular in the US and has inflicted economic harm on Americans. The MoU mediated by Qatar and Pakistan and signed last month aimed to create the conditions to bring the war to a permanent end. However, Tehran and Washington have since declared the accord “over” after accusing each other of violating it.
